# A ball with a two-limb center from an interval of two limbs

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_from_interval_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, that contains the interval $[l_o, h_i]$ of two values of `T`, with the exact midpoint for its center when halving is exact; or the whole line, or the empty set:

$$Z \supseteq [l_o, h_i].$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from_interval(lo, hi)` | `T`, `T` | `Ball<T, 2>` | `Ball<T, 2>::from_interval(lo, hi)`; the bounds are guarded ([rule R3](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)); `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $l_o$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $h_i$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball.
- If a bound is a NaN, whatever the other, or both are the same infinity ($[+\infty, +\infty]$, $[-\infty, -\infty]$): $Z$ is the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$).
- Otherwise, if the bounds are reversed, $l_o > h_i$: $Z$ is the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- Otherwise, if both are finite ($l_o \le h_i$): $Z$ is a finite ball that contains $[l_o, h_i]$.
- When moreover $l_o/2$ and $h_i/2$ are numbers of `T`: $c_w = (l_o + h_i)/2$ exactly and $r_w = \mathrm{RU}((h_i - l_o)/2)$, the smallest radius of `T` for that center.
- Otherwise ($l_o \le h_i$, $l_o < +\infty$, $h_i > -\infty$, and a bound is infinite): $Z$ is the whole line; a ball cannot be a half-line.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_from_interval_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_from_interval_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_from_interval_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the exact sum of the halves, and the difference of the halves rounded up (Milestone 2 listing; equal infinities the whole line, 2026-11-20). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_from_interval_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_from_interval_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum_ord`](two_sum_ord.md), [`add_up_1`](add_up_1.md).

```
# A ball with a 2-limb center from an interval [lo, hi] of two values of T supplied by the program,
# guarded (rule R3); milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface", "A ball from an interval of two T".
# The center is lo/2 + hi/2 as an exact 2-limb number, by two_sum_ord; the radius is
# RU(hi/2 - lo/2), the smallest radius of T for that center. When a halving is not exact (a bound
# that is an odd multiple of eta below 2N) the center may be off by eta, and the radius is the number
# after d = RU(hu - hl), the difference of the two rounded halves: at least d + eta, which is enough
# (with hu = hi/2 + a and hl = lo/2 + b, |a|, |b| <= eta/2, the radius needed is
# (hi - lo)/2 + |a + b| <= d - a + b + |a + b| <= d + eta). No constant of the listing is subnormal.
# The test of an exact halving doubles each half back by an exact product with 2, not by adding the
# half to itself, which GCC rewrites as a product it may fuse into the next addition. States: the
# whole line when a bound is a NaN, whatever the other bound, and when both bounds are the same
# infinity (decided on 2026-11-20, as for interval_make_1: a value from the program that is not
# finite never makes the empty set); otherwise the empty set for lo > hi (rv, false with a NaN);
# otherwise the whole line when a bound is infinite (a ball cannot be a half-line), and the ball
# above when both are finite. The difference of the halves adds minus the lower half, computed as
# its own exact product of the negated guarded bound, so that no fused result is negated (a rule of
# the generator); it is -hl, rounding to nearest being symmetric.

gl       = guard(lo)
gu       = guard(hi)
hl       = prod(gl, const up(1/2))
hu       = prod(gu, const up(1/2))
(c0, c1) = two_sum_ord(hl, hu)
gn       = neg(gl)
hn       = prod(gn, const up(1/2))
d        = add_up_1(hu, hn)
bl       = prod(hl, const up(2))
bu       = prod(hu, const up(2))
xl       = eq(bl, gl)
xu       = eq(bu, gu)
xx       = and(xl, xu)
dn       = succ(d)
r        = select(xx, d, dn)
ok       = le(gl, gu)
nl       = lt(gl, const inf)
mi       = neg(const inf)
nu       = lt(mi, gu)
va       = and(ok, nl)
v        = and(va, nu)
fl       = lt(mi, gl)
fu       = lt(gu, const inf)
f        = and(fl, fu)
k0       = select(f, c0, 0)
k1       = select(f, c1, 0)
s        = select(f, r, const inf)
rv       = lt(gu, gl)
wc       = select(rv, const nan, 0)
wr       = select(rv, const nan, const inf)
cw0      = select(v, k0, wc)
cw1      = select(v, k1, wc)
rw       = select(v, s, wr)
```

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
